subject: Re: Marketplace private offer pricing - unit price mapping and $/1M tokens target
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Zhang <claire.zhang@amazon.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@brightcart.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Marketplace private offer pricing - post-call recap + next steps

Hi Claire / Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on the private offer mapping and unit economics for BrightCart's use case: 

What we covered
- BrightCart expects ~50M–200M tokens/month in year 1, with burst windows up to ~1B tokens/month during holiday.
- Primary models: conversational text gen (chat) and reranking for search. Weighted avg token mix estimated: 60% generation, 40% embeddings/rerank.
- BrightCart's target effective spend: $600–$1,200 per 1M tokens (target price range for vendor-facing unit price after marketplace fees).

Ask / next steps (owners)
1) Claire: Can you confirm typical AWS Marketplace private offer fee/commission structure we should model (e.g., listing fee + marketplace cut) and whether AWS will accept a per-1M-token unit price in the private offer (we need it expressed as $/1M tokens).
2) Tom: Please confirm final committed monthly token volumes (range is fine) and whether BrightCart is open to a reserved-commit tier + burst pricing.
3) Rafael / Ben: I attached a preliminary unit-price mapping worksheet — please fill in effective unit price assumptions (Redwood list price, marketplace fee, final customer-facing unit price).

Attachments: marketplace_unit_price_mapping.xlsx (worksheet we reviewed), redwood_pricing_worksheet.xlsx (internal assumptions), aws_marketplace_private_offer_template.pdf

If we can get Claire's fee model + Tom's committed ranges by EOD Monday (23rd), I can draft a private offer price ladder (reserve tiers + burst rates) and circulate for signatures.

Thanks —
Marissa

From: Claire Zhang <claire.zhang@amazon.com>

Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer pricing - unit price mapping and $/1M tokens target

Hi Marissa / Tom —

Thanks for the summary — Claire from AWS Marketplace here. A few quick clarifications on the private offer structure: 

- AWS accepts custom pricing structures in private offers, and you can represent consumption as a unit price (we see this expressed as $/1M tokens frequently).
- Typical marketplace margin/fees depend on the channel/partner configuration; for standard AWS Marketplace private offers when AWS is the reseller, plan for ~5–12% marketplace fee plus any additional listing fees. If you route via a Marketplace SaaS integration partner, that partner may take an additional uplift.
- For modeling, assume a conservative 12% fee to start; we can tighten after we confirm channel/reseller setup.
- Private offers support multi-tier pricing (e.g., committed tier unit price + burst unit price) and term discounts for 12/24 month commitments.

I attached the private offer template and a brief note about how to express metered usage (you'll want to map tokens to a metering dimension and a 1M-token unit).

I'll also set up a short internal sync for Wednesday if you'd like me to loop in enablement for contract review.

Best,
Claire Zhang
Marketplace Partner Manager, AWS
claire.zhang@amazon.com

From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@brightcart.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Claire Zhang <claire.zhang@amazon.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Nov 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer pricing - unit price mapping and $/1M tokens target

Marissa / Claire —

Quick update from procurement and finance side: BrightCart can commit to the following initial bands if we can get unit economics in the target range you discussed:
- 50M tokens/mo committed for 12 months (baseline)
- Option to scale to 200M tokens/mo with a 2x reserved uplift in Q2 (we need burst defined as >200M)
- Budget: target effective spend of ~$800 / 1M tokens (this is our internal preferred target; we can stretch to $1,000 / 1M for a multi-year deal)

They also prefer a private offer executed via AWS Marketplace (direct private offer reseller) to simplify procurement — happy to proceed with that path.

Can you draft the private offer ladder and show the final effective unit prices after AWS fees? We'll need that for internal approval.

Thanks —
Tom
Head of Procurement | BrightCart
procurement@brightcart.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer pricing - internal calc and ask for marketplace fee sensitivity

Marissa / Ben —

I've filled the redwood_pricing_worksheet.xlsx with our baseline numbers and a few sensitivity scenarios. Highlights: 
- Redwood hosted list price (benchmark): $700 / 1M tokens (model mix adjusted); this is our go-to public list for similar workloads.
- To meet BrightCart target (effective $800 / 1M), we need to set a private offer unit price at ~$910 / 1M if AWS takes a 12% fee (910 - 12% = ~802).
- If AWS fee is lower (5%), private offer can be ~$842 / 1M to hit $800 effective.
- For a multi-tier ladder:
  * 50M/mo reserved: private-offer $930 / 1M -> effective to BrightCart (after 12% fee) ~$818 / 1M
  * 200M/mo reserved: private-offer $860 / 1M -> effective ~$757 / 1M
  * Burst (metered above commit): private-offer $1,050 / 1M -> effective ~$924 / 1M

Questions for Claire: can you confirm whether AWS fee is applied on the seller gross or net after discounts? That changes the mapping slightly. Also, if BrightCart wants a top-level $/1M on their invoice (instead of listing the AWS fee separately), we should confirm marketplace invoicing behavior for private offers.

Note: I also added a column for our internal unit economics (GPU cost per 1M tokens, infra, SRE/ops allowance) to ensure we maintain margin at each tier.

Rafael
Sr. Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai

- 50M/mo reserved (12-mo): private-offer $930 / 1M tokens -> BrightCart effective ~$818 / 1M (12% fee modeled)
- 200M/mo reserved (12-mo): private-offer $860 / 1M tokens -> BrightCart effective ~$757 / 1M
- Burst (>200M, metered): private-offer $1,050 / 1M tokens -> BrightCart effective ~$924 / 1M

- Tom: confirm you can sign a 12-mo commit for the 50M baseline and share procurement contact for DocuSign.
